run.question:
Can you help me check recent logs? We had a DR test in prod starting 6 hours ago.
companyopswebjob seemed to have some issues while a user was performing a test to
create a new scheduled job. It failed with 500s.
Please search the app-254-prod-logs index for relevant logs.

report.summary: The app-254-prod-logs index contains 12 documents inside the authorized window, timestamped 2026-11-20T23:34:58Z to 2026-11-21T04:34:58Z, carrying only the service labels Company.Ops (7) and Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob (5) and levels INFO=5, ERROR=5, WARN=2. They show the failure the user described: at 2026-11-21T02:34:58Z Company.Ops on ops-prod-02 logged 'Failed to create new scheduled job: HTTP 500 - transaction deadlock detected on jobs table' (correlation job-8831), preceded by a 500 'unable to acquire database lock during failover' at 00:34:58Z and a 503 'Job creation endpoint returning 503 - database failover in progress' at 01:34:58Z, and followed by recovery entries at 03:34:58Z and 04:34:58Z. The log text itself ties these errors to the DR failover that began at 23:34:58Z with a 'connection timeout to failover DB after 30s'. Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob has its own error logs naming Company.Ops as upstream. The exact name 'companyopswebjob' does not appear in any document returned and matches no Kubernetes workload; the similarly named entities that do exist are the log service labels Company.Ops and Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob. Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable, the failover database is never identified, and there is no pre-DR baseline in this index, so the conclusion is partial with root_cause null.

claims.text: app-254-prod-logs returned 12 documents whose timestamp lies inside the authorized window, spanning 2026-11-20T23:34:58Z to 2026-11-21T04:34:58Z, with levels INFO=5, ERROR=5, WARN=2, service labels only 'Company.Ops' (7) and 'Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob' (5), and hosts ops-prod-01 (5), radar-prod-01 (5), ops-prod-02 (2).
At 2026-11-20T23:34:58Z service 'Company.Ops' on host ops-prod-01 logged INFO correlation_id dr-test-001: 'DR test initiated - switching to failover database'.
At 2026-11-21T00:34:58Z service 'Company.Ops' (ops-prod-01, correlation dr-test-001) logged ERROR 'Job scheduler failed to process batch: connection timeout to failover DB after 30s'.
At 2026-11-21T00:34:58Z service 'Company.Ops' (ops-prod-01, correlation job-8827) logged ERROR 'Scheduled job execution failed with status 500: unable to acquire database lock during failover'.
At 2026-11-21T01:34:58Z service 'Company.Ops' on host ops-prod-02 logged WARN (correlation dr-test-001) 'Job creation endpoint returning 503 - database failover in progress'.

At 2026-11-21T02:34:58Z service 'Company.Ops' on host ops-prod-02 logged ERROR (correlation job-8831) 'Failed to create new scheduled job: HTTP 500 - transaction deadlock detected on jobs table'; this is the failed scheduled-job creation described by the user, with status 500.

Service 'Company.Ops' logged recovery: 2026-11-21T03:34:58Z INFO 'DR test failover completed - primary database restored' (dr-test-001, ops-prod-01) and 2026-11-21T04:34:58Z INFO 'Job scheduler resumed normal operation' (ops-prod-01).

Service 'Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob' on radar-prod-01 logged its own errors during the same window: 00:34:58Z 'Radar batch processing failed: upstream dependency Company.Ops unavailable during failover', 01:34:58Z 'Job execution error: HTTP 500 from internal API - database connection pool exhausted', 02:34:58Z WARN 'Retrying failed radar collection job after backoff', and 03:34:58Z INFO 'Radar data collection resumed successfully after failover recovery'.

The service aggregation over app-254-prod-logs for the authorized window shows only the labels 'Company.Ops' and 'Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob'; no service label resembling 'companyopswebjob' appears among the returned values.

The cluster holds no deployment named companyopswebjob: the 26 deployments returned are only kube-system, local-path-storage, otel-demo and app-100a workloads, none corresponding to the log services Company.Ops or Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob.

All Kubernetes events returned for the window are Normal events in namespace app-100a only — Deployment ScalingReplicaSet for loki and payment-api-100a, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, Pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started at 2026-11-21T05:33:21Z-05:33:45Z — and no returned event references any Company.Ops object.

The 500 on scheduled-job creation (job-8831, 02:34:58Z) most plausibly originates in the DR failover's database path: the messages attribute the failures to the failover ('unable to acquire database lock during failover', 'database failover in progress', 'connection timeout to failover DB after 30s'), and the errors stop after the failover-completed and scheduler-resumed entries. The failing component is referred to only as a 'failover DB', never named, so this remains a hypothesis rather than a located root cause.

An alternative candidate not excluded by these logs: pre-existing lock contention or connection-pool sizing on the jobs table ('transaction deadlock detected on jobs table', 'database connection pool exhausted') that the failover merely exposed; the index has no samples before 23:34:58Z inside the window, so there is no pre-DR baseline for deadlock or pool behaviour.

Rejected: fault injection via the otel-demo flagd config caused these failures. The ConfigMap flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) has every flag (productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad) at defaultVariant 'off' and targets only otel-demo services, none of which is Company.Ops or Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob.

The app-100a creations of loki and payment-api-100a at 2026-11-21T05:33:21Z-05:33:45Z are Normal starting events about an hour after the last Company.Ops error and after the logged failover completion; they carry no error reason and no tie to the Company.Ops 500s.

Obtain the failover database's own telemetry (connection counts, lock/deadlock metrics, availability) for 2026-11-20T23:34:58Z-2026-11-21T03:34:58Z, since the logs point to that dependency as failing but never identify it.

Retrieve complete request-level logs for correlation IDs job-8827, job-8831 and dr-test-001 from the application's own log store, because app-254-prod-logs provides only 12 hourly-cadence documents for the whole window and cannot show per-request counts or a pre-DR baseline.

gaps: The exact-name lookup for 'companyopswebjob' in app-254-prod-logs returned status no_data (0 documents) from a query_string search over service, message, host and correlation_id in the authorized window; an empty match shows only that this query matched nothing, not that the name is absent everywhere, and whether the alias maps to 'Company.Ops' or 'Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob' is unconfirmed.

Prometheus was unavailable during this Run: get_prometheus_target (job 'otel-collector'), get_label_values(service_name), get_metric_names and execute_prometheus_instant_query each returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, latency, resource or failover-DB metric baseline was read; missing series are unknown, not zero.
Jaeger was unavailable: traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no trace corroboration or parent-child call edges were obtainable for Company.Ops or Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob.

app-254-prod-logs holds only 12 documents, all at hourly cadence from 2026-11-20T23:34:58Z onward; there are no samples before the DR test start inside the window, so background error rate, deadlock frequency and pool utilisation before the incident are unknown.
The failing dependency is referred to only as a 'failover DB'/'failover database' in log text; its host, engine, identity and health are absent from every available source.
No Kubernetes object corresponds to Company.Ops or Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob (no such Deployment, no events), so their pod status, restarts and container logs are outside the available evidence.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so no history of config, database or deployment changes preceding the DR test could be checked.
next_steps: Collect the failover database's connection-pool, lock-wait and deadlock metrics for 2026-11-20T23:34:58Z-2026-11-21T03:34:58Z to confirm the database as the origin.
Pull full application logs for correlation IDs job-8827, job-8831 and dr-test-001, including DR runbook steps, to establish a request-level error rate and first failure time.
Review the DR procedure for jobs-table lock handling and connection-pool sizing so scheduled-job creation does not return 500 during failover.
